title: People Ops — Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Guide (2026)
author: Avery Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose:
This document is Redwood Inference’s canonical People Operations guide for hiring, new-employee onboarding, performance and feedback cycles, and day-to-day manager responsibilities. It is intended for hiring managers, interviewers, new hires, and people-ops partners.

Scope:
Applies to all full-time employees, contractors on >6 month engagements, and hiring teams across engineering, product, sales, and ops. Private-deployment or regulated-customer–facing roles may have supplemental requirements referenced in linked pages.

=== Table of contents ===
1. Hiring process overview
2. Interview loop & scorecard standards
3. Offer and acceptance
4. Onboarding: first-day, 30/60/90 plan, and access matrix
5. Performance & feedback cycles (ongoing, quarterly, annual)
6. Manager playbook: 1:1s, coaching, calibration, and promotions
7. Templates and checklists (copyable)
8. Ownership and references

---

1) Hiring process overview

Short intro: Redwood uses a standardized, bias-mitigating hiring workflow to balance speed and rigor. Hiring managers partner with People Ops to define role profiles, sourcing plans, interview loops and scorecards.

Key stages (owner in parentheses):
- Requisition & role definition (hiring manager + people-ops)
- Sourcing & screening (recruiter)
- Technical assessment / take-home (if applicable) (hiring manager)
- Interview loop (panel + scorecards) (interviewers + hiring manager)
- Final calibration & hire decision (hiring committee + people-ops)
- Offer & negotiation (recruiter + hiring manager)
- Onboarding & first 90 days (hiring manager + people-ops)

Minimum time targets:
- Requisition approval: ≤ 3 business days after request (people-ops review)
- First candidates in pipeline: ≤ 10 business days from approval (sourcing)
- Offer ext. after last onsites: ≤ 5 business days (recruiter)

Diversity & inclusion checkpoints:
- All roles must have at least one diverse-sourced candidate in the final 3 interviewed, when available.
- Interview panels should include at least one interviewer outside the immediate team for cross-functional perspective.

2) Interview loop & scorecard standards

Principles:
- Use structured interviews with rubric-based scorecards to reduce bias and accelerate decisioning.
- Each interviewer focuses on 1–2 competencies (e.g., system design, coding, product sense, communication, collaboration).

Standard loop (example for mid-senior SWE):
1. Recruiter screen (30 min) — culture fit, role expectations, salary band (recruiter)
2. Technical coding screen (45–60 min) — live pair coding or take-home (engineer)
3. System design (60 min) — architecture, tradeoffs, scalability (senior engineer/tech lead)
4. Cross-functional interview (45 min) — product sense / collaboration (product/pm)
5. Manager interview (45 min) — role alignment, growth & team fit (hiring manager)
6. Final calibration / hiring committee review (30–60 min) — decision & next steps (committee + people-ops)

Scorecard fields (required):
- Competency (string)
- Rating (1–5) and rationale (clear examples)
- Hire/no-hire recommendation (yes/maybe/no)
- Any known weaknesses and mitigation steps

Guidance for interviewers:
- Document concrete examples: what the candidate did that earned a rating.
- Avoid hypothetical-elusive questions and high-context trivia.
- If unsure, mark as 'needs calibration' and add notes for committee.

3) Offer and acceptance

Offer preparation checklist (recruiter + hiring manager):
- Confirm role level and comp band (people-ops published bands).
- Prepare stock grant recommendation and vesting schedule.
- Draft benefits overview and relocation/remote policy (if relevant).
- Legal check for contractor/visa constraints (finance-legal).

Negotiation principles:
- Start with the published band and justify exceptional variances based on market data and criticality.
- Keep HR/recruiter in the loop; final sign-off by people-ops required for above-band increases.

Decline & counteroffer handling:
- If a candidate declines, recruiter collects feedback and re-opens active shortlist.
- Counteroffers: hiring manager should not solicit counteroffers from candidate’s current employer; document any direct counteroffers in candidate record.

4) Onboarding

Intro: Goal for onboarding is to make new hires productive and connected by 30/60/90 days. Onboarding is a shared responsibility: people-ops runs org-level touchpoints; hiring managers own role-level ramp.

First-day checklist (to be completed by manager + IT + people-ops):
- Welcome email & org intro sent (people-ops)
- Manager 30-min welcome 1:1 scheduled (hiring manager)
- Workspace & hardware delivered and validated (IT)
- Account access provisioned (see access matrix table) (IT/security)
- New-hire orientation scheduled (people-ops)
- Buddy assigned and intro meeting scheduled (hiring manager)
- Payroll, benefits enrollment instructions sent (people-ops/finance)

Access matrix (required systems — copy and adapt):
| Area | Minimum access on day 1 | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Email & SSO | Full access | IT/security |
| Slack | Member | IT/people-ops |
| Code repo (read) | Read on relevant repos | Engineering infra |
| Jira/Asana | Productive access | Eng/product ops |
| Internal docs (Confluence) | Read/edit by team | Docs owner |
| Cloud console (prod no) | No prod access | Eng infra (request process) |

30/60/90 plan template (manager-owned):
- Day 1–30: Orientation, core skills, first small deliverable, team integrations, regular 1:1s twice weekly first 2 weeks then weekly.
- Day 31–60: Ownership of a small project, independent contributions, cross-team collaborations, mid-point feedback.
- Day 61–90: Lead a piece of work to completion, present learnings, performance checkpoint and goals for next quarter.

Buddy program:
- Purpose: socialization, context on team norms, and quick technical orientation.
- Buddy responsibilities: weekly check-ins first month, help with tooling, and social intro.

New-hire orientation agenda (people-ops, ~3 hours):
- Company mission & product overview
- Benefits walkthrough and payroll Q&A
- Security basics and data handling policies
- Slack/comms etiquette and org chart intro

5) Performance & feedback cycles

Principles:
- Emphasize continuous feedback; formal cycles create moments for calibration and career discussion.
- Managers own performance conversations; people-ops supports calibration, training, and process integrity.

Cadence and timeline:
- Continuous ongoing 1:1s (recommended weekly) — coaching, blockers, small feedback.
- Quarterly check-ins (informal written summary + 1:1) — progress on goals, development.
- Annual performance review (formal) — ratings, compensation changes, promotion recommendations.

Annual review process (summary):
1. Self-assessment submission (employee) — due 2 weeks before manager review window.
2. Manager assessment and calibration notes (manager) — due 1 week before calibration.
3. Calibration meeting (cross-team leads + people-ops) — normalize ratings and promotion decisions.
4. Compensation recommendations (people-ops + finance) — apply budget and merit rules.
5. Manager delivers feedback & outcome (manager) — conversation and documentation in HRIS.

Rating scale (example):
- 1: Below expectations — requires improvement plan
- 2: Partially meets expectations — inconsistent delivery
- 3: Meets expectations — solid, reliable contribution
- 4: Exceeds expectations — high impact and leadership in area
- 5: Exceptional — sustained transformative impact

Promotion and leveling guidance:
- Promotions require demonstrable scope growth, consistent >4 ratings across multiple cycles or strong calibration evidence.
- Promotions should include concrete examples of ownership and outcomes.

Performance improvement plans (PIP):
- Trigger: sustained <2 ratings or major policy/behavioral incidents.
- PIP steps: define outcomes (30–90 days), measurable milestones, weekly check-ins, HR oversight, and a final decision at plan completion.

6) Manager playbook: core responsibilities and templates

Manager responsibilities (summary):
- Hiring: write role profile, interview, make hiring recommendation.
- Onboarding: run first 90-day plan and assign buddy.
- Performance: weekly 1:1s, quarterly check-ins, annual reviews and career conversations.
- Culture & compliance: ensure team follows security, data handling, and code review policies.

Running effective 1:1s (recommended structure):
- Regular cadence: weekly 30–60 min.
- Agenda template (share before the meeting):
  - Wins & highlights (5 min)
  - Roadblocks & support needed (10–15 min)
  - Career/development talk (10 min)
  - Admin & housekeeping (5–10 min)

Giving feedback guidance (RAD framework):
- Recognize — state what you observed.
- Amplify or Adjust — describe impact and the desired change.
- Discuss — invite the employee’s perspective and agree on next steps.

Career development: growing a team member
- Create development goals that are specific, measurable, and timebound.
- Pair on stretch projects and shadowing opportunities.
- Track progress in quarterly check-ins and support training budget requests via people-ops.

Promotion recommendation template (manager):
- Candidate name, current level, proposed level
- Examples of impact (3–5 bullet points with metrics/outcomes)
- Scope increase and leadership signals
- Calibration comments and reviewer endorsements

7) Templates and checklists (copyable)

New-hire first-week agenda (example):
- Day 1: Orientation, team lunch, tool access validation, 1:1 with manager
- Day 2: Product deep-dive, shadowing, set first tasks
- Day 3: Technical onboarding (repos, CI, infra walkthrough)
- Day 4: Cross-team intros and scheduled learning time
- Day 5: First-week retrospective with manager and buddy

Interview scorecard example (text):
- Competency: System design
- Rating (1–5): 4
- Notes: Candidate described tradeoffs between consistency and availability and proposed a partitioning strategy with caching; follow-up question uncovered limited experience with distributed transactions.

Sample 30-day manager check-in email subject: "30-day sync — [Name]"
Body template: "Hi [Name], congrats on 30 days. Let’s review your wins, blockers, and goals for next 60 days. Please prepare a 10-min update and 3 learning goals."
